newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ATHERTON SHOULD BE DROPPED, ILLINGWORTH SAYS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON SHOULD BE DROPPED, ILLINGWORTH SAYS.

text.p: Mike Atherton should be axed as England captain for the one-day internationals against Australia this year, according to his former chairman of selectors Ray Illingworth.
Illingworth wrote in Tuesday's Express newspaper that current chairman David Graveney should give less experienced members of the side a chance to lead the side.

"Atherton's leadership of the England side has never been truly convincing," said Illingworth, who stepped down as chairman of selectors last year. "But there have been almost no alternatives in the past few years.
"That is not the case now. Nasser Hussain, his vice-captain on the winter tour of Zimbabwe and New Zealand, and Adam Hollioake, the A team skipper, have the potential to lead the side with panache.
"Graveney should bite the bullet, show some boldness and axe Atherton as England's one-day captain in favour of either Hussain or Hollioake."
Graveney responded by saying he did not favour appointing two captains -- one for the one-day internationals and one for the Ashes test series.
He said he would consult former England captains Graham Gooch and Mike Gatting -- both now England selectors -- before making a decision on the captaincy in the next few weeks.
"My view is that we should have the same captain for both particular elements," he said.
"Ray, whom I've learned a lot from during my two years as selector, has had his time and now it's down to the three of us to decide what is the right course for England to take."
England face Australia in three one-day internationals in May and in the six-test Ashes series in July and August.
